text:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing NCCL handshake timeouts on multi-GPU training in eu-west-1 (pool-gpu-a). Jobs hit allreduce failures during shuffle-heavy steps and restart. Only affects some nodes, looks east-west heavy. Logs show `NCCL WARN CONNECTION` + `ibv_rc_pingpong` failures.

ashok: Which hosts? any pattern (rack, switch, NIC model)?

maria: Affected host pairs: gw-eu-03 <-> gw-eu-07 and gw-eu-04 <-> gw-eu-08. All are A100s but gw-eu-07/08 are on a different rack/switch. Same jobs run fine when pinned to same host (intra-node).

kai: Can you paste `dmesg` / mlx5 logs and `ethtool -i` / `ibv_devinfo`? Also check MTU and rp_filter. Those often bite RoCE v2 setups.

maria: Pasting abbreviated outputs: 

```
# on gw-eu-03
$ ethtool -i ens2f0
driver: mlx5_core
firmware-version: 22.26.1240

$ ip link show ens2f0
3: ens2f0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000

# on gw-eu-07
$ ip link show ens2f0
3: ens2f0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000

# sysctl rp_filter
net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 1
net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter = 1
net.ipv4.conf.ens2f0.rp_filter = 1  # on gw-eu-03
net.ipv4.conf.ens2f0.rp_filter = 0  # on gw-eu-07
```

maria: So MTU mismatch (9000 vs 1500) + rp_filter differs. Not sure which one is primary cause.

ashok: MTU mismatch can definitely break RoCE v2 if jumbo frames are expected. Also rp_filter=1 on one side can drop packets if reply path uses different interface. Were there recent config pushes?

netops-bot: Rollout alert: kernel 5.10.102-1 rolled to eu-west-1 hosts at 2026-03-12T03:12:00Z (gw-eu-03..gw-eu-10). No network policy changes recorded.

dana: We also applied a switch firmware update on rack B (where gw-eu-07/08 live) last night. Could have reset MTU defaults on the leaf.

kai: Quick repro: try `ibv_rc_pingpong -d mlx5_0 -s 1024` between the two nodes while toggling MTU/rp_filter. If pingpong fails with fragmentation/errors it's the MTU. If unidirectional drops align with rp_filter, you'll see ICMP/LOG entries.

ashok: For quick mitigation, set rp_filter=0 and force MTU to a common value (9000) on both endpoints for the test. We can do ephemeral change via `sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0` and `ip link set dev ens2f0 mtu 9000` on the 1500 side. Be careful on other services; schedule off-hours.

maria: Did the ephemeral change on gw-eu-07 (set mtu 9000 + rp_filter=0) — restarted the job. Handshake completes now, allreduce proceeds. :tada:

ashok: Great. That suggests both factors matter — the switch reverted MTU and rp_filter strictness prevented asymmetric replies. We need a proper fix: audit all eu-west NIC/switch MTU consistency, pin RoCE VLANs, and standardize rp_filter configuration (recommend 2/loose or 0 for our RDMA paths).

dana: I'll open a ticket with NetOps to confirm switch MTU persisted settings and to schedule a maintenance window to align MTU on rack B. Also will check if the kernel rollout toggled rp_filter defaults.

maria: Filing incident ticket INC-2026-01923 with logs and the quick mitigation steps. Leaving the temp rp_filter change in place on affected nodes until netops confirms.

kai: Follow-up action items: 1) cluster-wide MTU audit script, 2) enforce rp_filter=0 in our RDMA host profile, 3) add an NCCL handshake SLO alarm (rate of handshake failures), 4) doc runbook for asymmetric routing + RoCE.

ashok: I'll own the runbook and the rp_filter host-profile PR. Thanks team.

maria: Thanks — happy to help with validation after netops changes.
